results.notes: Reproduction is of the printed, unadjusted arm descriptives at one decimal place, using the authors' deposited dyad scores; the original text-to-score pipeline is not rerun. Both meeting modalities are pooled, cue is treatment, and no cue is control. The reproduced SDs are across dyads, with denominator n_dyads-1. No participant-attributed ideas, topic labels, or individual scores are deposited. Therefore the requested participant-level SD fields are null: copying each shared dyad score to two invented individual records would not recover those scores. The reported means and difference are in the original shared-dyad outcome units. All dyads contain two people (PDF p. 5, printed p. 300, section 4.1.1), so equal-dyad and equal-person weighting of the shared outcome yield identical means. People counts are twice the observed dyad counts, not counts of ideas, ratings, or post-survey responses. Study roster checks compare the 86 distinct session rows and their 172 dyad members with the printed study totals; they do not establish the paper's outcome-specific analysis counts, which are not printed. The post surveys have a missing response and duplicate participant labels (S67P1 and S22P1) and are not used as an exclusion rule or as a unique-person roster. No missing score or background covariate is imputed. Missing design/recycling covariates are retained for these outcome-available descriptives and the new unadjusted contrast. The paper's REML models instead exclude missing covariates and use cue, modality, and their interaction as fixed effects plus design and recycling knowledge as random effects. The REML F statistics, denominator degrees of freedom, and p values are not claimed reproduced. Standard errors below come from OLS of one shared dyad score on an intercept and cue indicator, clustered by Session with CR1 correction G/(G-1)*(N-1)/(N-2), N=G. These are new raw contrasts on the samples reproducing the descriptives, not the paper's covariate-complete adjusted model. This is a between-dyad design, so no first_round result applies. Source: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 302), sections 4.1.4 and 5.1.1; Supplementary Data README.txt defines Topic diversity as Shannon entropy of topics from the dyad's ideas. The source file has 86 distinct session rows. Missing outcomes are S5, S15, leaving 84 dyads (41 cue, 43 no cue; 82 and 86 people). The source includes sessions S1-S88 except S51 and S86; no outcome or participant is invented for missing identifiers. The paper's descriptions of technical/echo exclusions cannot be linked to additional session IDs, so no further sessions are dropped. Missing background covariates occur in 13 dyad rows: S1, S2, S5, S6, S7, S9, S10, S12, S17, S18, S26, S29, S35. Section 4.1.1 refers to 13 participants rather than 13 dyads; this file does not identify which member lacked covariates. Restricting to complete covariates would leave 72 dyads (34 cue, 38 no cue) with means 2.303655824235 and 2.089900357421, SDs 0.285386291924 and 0.387497563483. Those also round to the printed descriptives, so the printed precision cannot uniquely identify the idea descriptive sample. The result uses all observed scores, consistently with the conversation descriptives; it is explicitly not asserted to recover the REML sample. No individual topic assignments or embedding model are in the deposit, so only the supplied entropy scores and their arm summaries are verified. This within-dyad flexibility outcome is distinct from the unavailable across-dyad homogenization measure. Observed cells: cue/inperson=20, cue/virtual=21, no cue/inperson=21, no cue/virtual=22.

Source: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 304), section 5.1.2; PDF p. 7 (printed p. 302), section 4.1.4 and footnote 12; Supplementary Data README.txt. Topic_diversity is the number of distinct broad IAB topics across the entire dyad conversation. All 66 deposited conversation rows have scores: 29 cue and 37 no cue dyads, representing 58 and 74 people. The 66 rows are compatible with footnote 12's 70 recordings and 4 echo exclusions, but the footnote's additional 16 recordings and the exclusions in section 4.1.1 do not establish an unambiguous complete flow of participants; counts here come from the deposited sessions, not subtraction from the recruited total or model degrees of freedom. Missing covariates occur in 11 rows: S10, S17, S18, S1, S26, S29, S2, S35, S6, S7, S9. Complete-covariate analysis would use 55 dyads (22 cue, 33 no cue; 44 and 66 people), with means 9.727272727273 and 8.060606060606, SDs 2.333642527442 and 2.621299700761; these round to 9.7, 8.1, 2.3, and 2.6 and do not reproduce the printed 9.6, 8.0, 2.2, and 2.5. The descriptives therefore identify the outcome-available sample rather than the sample excluding missing background covariates. No transcription or IAB classification is rerun because only the final scores are posted. Observed cells: cue/inperson=16, cue/virtual=13, no cue/inperson=18, no cue/virtual=19.

Reproduction failed; no requested effect statistics are calculated. The '# of all ideas' column is the README-defined dyad idea count. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 302), section 5, prints an overall mean of 19.4 ideas. The 84 nonmissing rows (S5 and S15 missing) sum to 1653 ideas and give 19.678571428571, rounding to 19.7 rather than 19.4. Applying the stated covariate exclusion leaves 72 dyads and gives 19.902777777778, rounding to 19.9. No additional exclusion IDs or analysis code are supplied that resolve the mismatch. PDF p. 9 (printed p. 304), section 5.1.3, prints only a verbal non-significance conclusion, with no arm means, difference/coefficient, test statistic, p value, or analyzed arm counts; thus even the minimum arm-contrast reproduction check has no numerical target. The failed checks are retained as an analyzed result for audit, with every computed field null. This record is not counted as a reproduced estimate and is not duplicated in skipped.

skipped.reason: Cannot follow the paper's semantic-diversity procedure exactly. The deposit contains only dyad summary outcomes and post-survey responses; it has no human idea texts, idea embeddings, cosine distances, or text-to-dyad mapping. The embedding model is not named, and PDF p. 11 (printed p. 306), section 6.3, describes condition-specific centroids whereas PDF p. 16 (printed p. 311), Appendix A.4.1, describes an average across Cue and NoCue ideas. PDF p. 17 (printed p. 312), Figure 6, has distributions only, with no printed human-arm means, counts, Wilcoxon statistic, or numerical uncertainty to reproduce. No embedding model or centroid convention is guessed, no values are taken from plotted positions, and no participant-level values or standardized effect are assigned to this set-based measure.
